question.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $15{x}_{2},$ where ${x}_{2}$ is the second component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\},\,x=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -15\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{2},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{2}}{{q}_{2}\cdot {q}_{2}} \\  & =\frac{10\cdot 4+(-15)\cdot 3}{{4}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{40-45}{25} \\  & =\frac{-5}{25} \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
15{x}_{2}=15\cdot (-\frac{1}{5})=-3.
$$
